design.text: Randomized, open-label, multicenter, global comparative trial evaluating tremelimumab plus durvalumab (T300+D), durvalumab monotherapy, and sorafenib.

citations.quote: HIMALAYA is a randomized, open-label, multicenter, global trial which evaluated tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab (T300+D), durvalumab monotherapy and sorafenib in 1171 patients with previously untreated, unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC).

population.text: Patients with previously untreated, unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC).

citations.quote: HIMALAYA is a randomized, open-label, multicenter, global trial which evaluated tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab (T300+D), durvalumab monotherapy and sorafenib in 1171 patients with previously untreated, unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC).

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS) superiority of T300+D versus sorafenib.

citations.quote: The primary objective was to demonstrate the overall survival (OS) superiority of T300+D versus sorafenib.

n.text: N=1171 randomized in the analysis population; T300+D 393, durvalumab 389, sorafenib 389.

citations.quote: durvalumab monotherapy and sorafenib in 1171 patients with previously untreated, unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC).

result.text: T300+D showed statistically significant OS improvement versus sorafenib: median OS 16.4 vs 13.8 months; HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.66, 0.92); 2-sided p=0.0035.

citations.quote: HIMALAYA demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in OS in patients randomized to the T300+D arm compared to those who were randomized to the sorafenib arm (stratified hazard ratio [HR] of 0.78 [95% CI: 0.66, 0.92], stratified log-rank 2-sided p-value = 0.0035).

indication.text: IMJUDO, in combination with durvalumab, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC).

target_moa.text: Tremelimumab is a CTLA-4 blocking antibody that binds CTLA-4 and blocks its interaction with ligands CD80 and CD86, releasing CTLA-4-mediated inhibition of T-cell activation.

citations.quote: Tremelimumab is a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 (CTLA-4) blocking antibody that binds to CTLA-4 and blocks the interaction with its ligands CD80 and CD86, releasing CTLA-4-mediated inhibition of T-cell activation.
Tremelimumab (CP-675,206, MEDI1123) is an IgG2 monoclonal antibody directed against cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen-4 (CTLA-4).

requirement.text: 4333-1: Conduct Study D419EC00001, a Phase I/II open-label study to evaluate safety, PK, and preliminary efficacy of tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab in pediatric patients from birth to <18 years with relapsed/refractory malignant solid tumors or hematological malignancy.

citations.quote: 4333-1 Conduct Study D419EC00001 (A Phase I/II, open-label, multicenter study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy of tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab in pediatric patients) to further characterize the safety, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy of tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab in patients from birth to <18 years of age with relapsed/refractory malignant solid tumors or a relapsed/refractory hematological malignancy including lymphomas for whom no standard treatment is available. Include at least 12 patients in the dose escalation cohort and at least 45 evaluable patients in the dose expansion cohort.
